messages:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — I'm drafting the rollout spec for the model-routing V2 change (canary + A/B). Need to lock: version pinning rules for customers, canary sample size/duration, rollback criteria, and experiment metrics.
Arpit Singh: high level OK. propose canary = 1% of traffic for 24 hours, then 10% for 48 hours if green. enterprise customers pinned by default unless they opt in.
Jess Carter: +1 on pin-by-default for enterprise. Also need an engineer-facing flag so we can force-route a tenant for debugging.
Samir Rao: Agreed. For SLOs: p95 latency delta < 10% and error rate delta < 0.1pp vs v1. If either breached, auto-rollback.
Elaine Wong: For quality, we should run the production eval suite (the 2k prompt set) asynchronously and gate on BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and a human review threshold for any regression > 1.5%.
Maya Patel: Good. Can we capture exact acceptance criteria? I'll draft then we can iterate.
Arpit Singh: Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- infra: canary deployment at 1% for 24h with healthy checks passing.
- telemetry: no increase in 5xxs or internal errors > 0.1pp.
- latency: p95 increase <= 10% and median increase <= 5%.
- cost: tokens-per-request change <= 5% or flagged.
- quality: automated eval delta <= 1.5% AND no manual review rejects in sample of 100 checks.
Jess Carter: Add a guard: if any internal downstream service sees > 5% increase in request count (e.g., cache thrash), pause rollout.
Samir Rao: Rollback triggers: infra health failures, SLO breach, tombstone rate spike, or data-exfil detection from logs. Rollback should be automated but with a page to oncall.
Maya Patel: Experiment design: A/B (10/90) for 7 days after canary. Metrics to compute: UPLIFT on accuracy, change in p95, change in cost per 1k tokens, and user-level retention proxy (successful completions).
Elaine Wong: For statistical power, run uplift calc — need minimum N of 6k requests per cohort for primary metric. If we can't reach that, extend duration rather than increasing percent.
Arpit Singh: Version pinning: customers on Dedicated/Private remain pinned to v1 unless they opt into 'beta-routing'. Hosted customers default to auto-upgrade but can opt-out via tenant setting. We must log opt-in/out and enforce via routing table config.
Jess Carter: Also, add rollout escape hatch: feature flag to route 100% back to v1 instantly, with a manual confirmation from SRE before scaling back up.
Maya Patel: Edge cases: long-tail prompts causing memory growth, tokenization differences, incompatibility with cached prefixes — add preflight tests that run a small synthetic burst to validate KV cache behaviour.
Samir Rao: Monitoring: dashboards for p50/p95/p99, error rate, token-cost, cache hit ratio, worker GPU memory, and OOM counts. Alerts: p95 > threshold OR 5xx rate spike OR OOM > 1 in 1h.
Maya Patel: Deploy bot: schedule canary rollout once approval thread is closed and infra signoff done.
deploy-bot: scheduled rollout for 1748300000; requires approvals from @Maya_Patel @Arpit_Singh @Samir_Rao before proceeding.
Jess Carter: Launch checklist (short): PRD linked, infra smoke tests green, canary playbook written, runbook + rollback steps, monitoring dashboards, opt-in optics for enterprise, legal sign-off if data-handling changed.
Maya Patel: I'll post a draft PRD by EOD with acceptance criteria and the canary playbook. Please review and flag any missed edge cases.
Elaine Wong: One more: add a small human-in-the-loop daily review during the 10% phase for first 48h.
Arpit Singh: noted. I'll add the routing config snippet to the RFC:
```
routing: {
  default: v2,
  overrides: [
    { tenant: "enterprise-*", version: v1, pinned: true }
  ],
  experiment: { name: "v2_ab", percent: 10 }
}
```
Maya Patel: Thanks — will incorporate. If no objections by EOD I'll request approvals and schedule the deploy. :thumbsup:
